subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit, daily, and idle resets, and what default/config/security contract should govern it?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects latency, cost, silent agent execution, provider/auth selection, sensitive memory persistence, and plugin boundaries, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Approve guarded opt-in pre-reset flush
options.body: Add a reset-scoped agentic flush behind an explicit or clearly documented config/policy with timeout, dedupe, sandbox, consent, and audit requirements.

options.title: Keep reset persistence mechanical
options.body: Treat session-memory/reset-hook improvements as the supported reset boundary and narrow this issue away from silent tool-capable agent execution.

options.title: Delegate to memory plugins
options.body: Require memory plugins or MCP-backed services to own continuous persistence and extend core lifecycle APIs only where current hooks are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded opt-in pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Add a reset-scoped agentic flush behind an explicit or clearly documented config/policy with timeout, dedupe, sandbox, consent, and audit requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined history on both the existing pre-compaction flush primitive and `/new` reset behavior that this decision spans.
